name: Segment CT automatically (TotalSegmentator)
summary: Segments organs, bones, vessels and muscles in any CT (NIfTI, NRRD, MHA or DICOM series) with TotalSegmentator, and writes each case as <case>/ct.nii.gz + <case>/segmentations/<structure>.nii.gz, the
help: Wire any CT scans into Scans: a dataset of NIfTI files (one per case, or <case>/ct.nii.gz), NRRD/MHA volumes, or the files of DICOM series (one series per folder). Masks already in segmentations/ folders and label maps are skipped, so a dataset that comes with expert labels can be wired too. Wire Cases to Expert labels to 3D models, CT volume for the 3D view, Soft body model and Read medical images exactly as the expert labels were wired: they read the same layout. The first run on a worker downloads the network's weights (about 1.2 GB for the total task) into the worker's ~/.totalsegmentator; the next runs use them. Run on auto or NVIDIA GPU: the block goes to a worker with an NVIDIA GPU (about 1–3 minutes a case at 1.5 mm); CPU: any worker, about 12–15 minutes a case at 1.5 mm (3 mm: a few minutes). Usage statistics of TotalSegmentator are turned off. For research and teaching, not for clinical use. TotalSegmentator (Wasserthal et al., Radiology: AI 2023), Apache-2.0; only its open tasks are offered.

inputs.label: Scans
inputs.help: CT volumes (NIfTI, NRRD, MHA) or the files of DICOM series; masks in segmentations/ folders are skipped

outputs.label: Segmented cases
outputs.help: <case>/ct.nii.gz and <case>/segmentations/<structure>.nii.gz (one mask per structure), as the TotalSegmentator dataset lays them out

outputs.label: Structures found
outputs.help: segmentation.csv: case, structure, voxels, volume_ml, task, seconds

params.label: Task
params.help: total: 117 structures of a CT (organs, bones, vessels, muscles); total_mr: for MR scans; the others add detail to one region

params.label: Resolution
params.help: total, total_mr and body only. 3 mm is several times faster and fine for big organs; thin structures (ribs, small vessels) lose detail

params.label: Only these structures
params.help: total / total_mr: names separated by commas (liver, spleen, kidney_left, aorta…); the network then runs only on the part of the scan it needs. Empty: all

params.label: Run on
params.help: auto and NVIDIA GPU: the block goes only to a worker with an NVIDIA GPU (auto still falls back to the CPU if PyTorch cannot use it); CPU: any worker, slower

params.label: Scan file name
params.help: Which volumes are the scans (a pattern such as ct.nii.gz or *.nrrd); empty: every volume that is not a mask or a label map

params.label: Keep empty masks
params.help: The network writes a mask for every structure of the task, also those outside the scan; off: only the structures it found
